Software Development Engineer, SCOT-Inbound, Inventory Routing and Replenishment
jobs.description:
We are thrilled to have a Software Development Engineering opening for you in the Dice Team! As part of the Dice team you’ll work on the most advanced systems in Inventory Placement. We protect inventory availability for customer delivery speed, manage inventory balance between FCs, and we replenish inventory to our growing networks that include domestic and international marketplaces! We do all that with lead time and supply chain variability as core aspects of our optimization modeling.

As a member of our team you’ll be able to contribute directly to our customer’s experience with the Amazon supply chain, as well as reduce fulfillment cost and maximize free cash flow, across all worldwide marketplaces! But wait, there’s more! Inventory Placement has dedicated Analytics, Operational Research resources and you’ll get the unique opportunity of working with as part of our team.

This role might be for you if…
- You thrive on solving textbook-less problems
- You use object-oriented design concepts to program large multi-tier systems. You have working knowledge of common and useful design patterns.
- You have designed, launched, refactored, re-architected, deprecated and/or implemented large-scale cloud-based distributed services with millisecond latency and ultra-high transactional volumes.
- You design at the product level with heavy involvement through all phases of the SDLC using concepts that may include Service Oriented Architecture, caching, load balancing, non-relational databases, microservices, sharding, n-tiered architecture, cloud and/or map-reduce.
- You have experience implementing best practices in improving team coding culture related to quality and/or security.
- Effectively articulate technical challenges and solutions to non-technical audiences.


Key job responsibilities
In this job, you will…
- Experiment with whatever technology we need to get the job done.
- Use Lean Software Development concepts such as Agile, Scrum and Kanban.
- Use Test-Driven Development and Continuous Deployment.
- Work with Senior and Principal Engineers, Researchers, and Data Engineers across multiple teams to design a new platform for optimizing supply chain management
- Expand and optimize our world-class supply chain systems to support a variety of emerging business initiatives.
- Automate third party supply management systems and break new ground to drive inventory across Amazon marketplaces.

Are you excited by being able to have Amazon deliver items to your front door within hours? Are you fascinated by Amazon’s ability to combine your online shopping into fewer boxes and shipments? All of these amazing customer experiences are possible because of Inventory Placement – we get the right inventory to the right place, at the right time!

A day in the life
Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment.

The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:
- Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
- Maternity and Parental Leave Options
- Paid Time Off (PTO)
- 401(k) Plan

If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you!

At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Amazon ECS
jobs.description:
Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) is a fully managed container orchestration service that helps you easily deploy, manage, and scale containerized applications. The ECS team develops features that impact thousands of users and customers both internally and externally!

Amazon ECS is looking for a Software Development Engineer (SDE) to deliver our container orchestration service and accelerate adoption of containers in the cloud. This role includes responsibility for ECS and Fargate, our Serverless container compute offering. We are seeking an SDE with strong knowledge of distributed systems. You must enjoy working on complex software systems in a customer-centric environment and be passionate not only about building good software but also ensuring that the same software achieves its goals in operational reality.

A successful candidate will need a strong understanding of software development with Linux, and be comfortable analyzing large amounts of data from multiple sources within a distributed network.
- Create a first-class experience for our customers by keeping their needs at the center of your work.
- Solve difficult problems with elegant and practical code.
- Design, build, deploy, and own scalable and robust systems, taking well scoped requirements through to delivery.
- Help operate a public AWS service, including participating in on-call and improving operational health.
- Use data to guide your decisions and validate your assumptions.
- Contribute to architecture and technology choices for your features, and grow into a broader technical voice over time.
- Develop project plans and commitments, and deliver consistently against them.

To learn more about Amazon Elastic Container Service: https://aws.amazon.com/ecs

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer III, Android
jobs.description:
At Audible, we believe stories have the power to transform lives. It’s why we work with some of the world’s leading creators to produce and share audio storytelling with our millions of global listeners. We are dreamers and inventors who come from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences to empower and inspire each other. Imagine your future with us.

ABOUT THE TEAM
As a Software Development Engineer III within the Audible Android team, you can help us innovate, develop, and deliver continued expansion of this much-loved product. If you have an interest in working on an application that reaches millions of loyal customers on a daily bases, then the Android Apps team at Audible might be for you.

ABOUT THIS ROLE
As a Software Development Engineer III, it’s up to you to define, design and refine the tech that keeps us one step ahead of listeners. Anticipate. Innovate. Bring challenging ideas and we’ll support you with the latest tech, tools, and systems that you need to succeed. jobs.title: Senior Software Development Engineer , Service Resource Management
jobs.description:
Amazon's global Customer Service network serves hundreds of millions of customers, and the decisions behind how that network runs matter. The Service Resource Management team is building a network optimization product that helps leaders review performance with more clarity, understand what is driving drift from plan, make better site and resource decisions, and trust automation where repeatable decisions allow it. We are hiring a Senior Software Development Engineer to help define how the product, the system, and the engineering approach scale together as the team and problem space grow. In this role, you will set direction in ambiguous spaces, challenge weak assumptions, and create clarity when the obvious answer may be wrong. You will lead multi-engineer efforts, shape technical judgment across the team, make trade-offs visible, and decide when AI-assisted techniques, rules, or human review are the right mechanism for the problem.

Key job responsibilities
- Set technical direction across multiple workflows and components, including service boundaries, data contracts, system observability, operator-facing product behavior, and the visibility of key trade-offs.
- Lead multi-engineer projects from problem framing through design, delivery, rollout, and post-launch follow-through, deciding where simple rules, AI-assisted analysis, or statistical methods are appropriate and keeping solutions explainable and proportionate.
- Shape automation boundaries so predictable decisions are handled by systems and human judgment is reserved for exceptional cases, while defining where the system should stay flexible by default versus where specialization is justified by measurable value.
- Influence related teams and dependent systems when upstream or downstream decisions affect product correctness, speed, or trustworthiness, and drive simplification in both system design and team operating model.
- Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, hiring, mentoring, and clear written decision-making that helps the team grow.

A day in the life
A typical day mixes technical direction, design judgment, and organizational influence. You might review a design that spans multiple systems, work through an ambiguous network problem with product and engineering partners, and help the team decide whether a problem calls for simplification, automation, deeper analysis, or a change in operating mechanism. You will also spend time coaching other engineers and making sure important decisions stay explainable, durable, and grounded in evidence.

About the team
The Service Resource Management team builds products that help Amazon Customer Service leaders make better decisions about how the global network runs. We want to be a team that can talk about hard things clearly and early. That means creating the conditions for open disagreement, surfacing weak assumptions before they harden into direction, making trade-offs explicit, and leaving important decisions with shared understanding, clear ownership, and follow-through.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer , Service Resource Management
jobs.description:

Our work helps leaders review network performance with more clarity, understand what is driving drift from plan, make better site and resource decisions, and use automation where repeatable decisions can be trusted.

In this role, you will own meaningful parts of the product end to end and work across service behavior, data logic, and product experience to make leadership review, network analysis, and day-to-day operating decisions clearer, faster, and more actionable.

We are looking for an engineer who can make sound decisions with incomplete information, turn partially defined problems into reliable solutions, and improve systems by fixing causes rather than symptoms. You should be comfortable bringing facts, tradeoffs, and risks into the conversation and helping move important decisions toward clear follow-through. Because the team is building toward a more AI-native way of operating, you should also be comfortable evaluating where AI-assisted analysis, automation, rules, and conventional software each fit best in a production workflow.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the design and delivery of one or more workflows or subsystems, such as analytics services, anomaly-review experiences, investigation tooling, data quality controls, or operator-facing product flows
- Build reliable backend systems and supporting jobs that turn internal data into clear and trustworthy product behavior, and automate repeatable decision paths where the evidence is strong enough to do so safely
- Define and document metric logic, edge-case handling, operational behavior, and design tradeoffs so other engineers and business partners can understand, question, and extend your area
- Improve observability, data quality, and operational health, and remove recurring pain points by fixing root causes rather than treating symptoms
- Partner with product, domain stakeholders, and peer engineers to clarify requirements, surface tradeoffs early, and turn them into implementation plans
- Mentor newer engineers through code reviews, design feedback, debugging support, and day-to-day collaboration.
- Contribute to workflows that use AI-assisted analysis or automation where it improves clarity, speed, or decision quality

A day in the life
A typical day in this role is a mix of ownership, technical judgment, and follow-through. You might spend part of the day driving a subsystem change from design through implementation, tracing an issue across service behavior and the underlying data path, and working with product or domain partners to decide what action is justified by the evidence. You will also spend time improving the clarity of the system itself, whether that means simplifying a workflow, tightening a metric definition, or making a recommendation easier for leaders to trust.

About the team
The Service Resource Management team builds products that help Amazon Customer Service leaders make better decisions about how the global network runs. We want to be a team that can talk about hard things clearly and early. At this level, that means bringing facts, tradeoffs, and risks into the conversation, challenging assumptions respectfully, moving quickly without outrunning the evidence, and helping the team leave important discussions with clear decisions and durable follow-through.

Our mission: enable developers to build communities around live video. We handle everything from ingest to processing to delivery at global scale, so developers can focus on creating interactive, engaging live experiences for their audiences. Whether you're streaming to tens of millions of concurrent viewers or just getting started, Amazon IVS removes the complexity so developers can move fast.

The IVS Stream Management team builds and operates the distributed systems that coordinate stream sessions end-to-end and keep the underlying fleet healthy under bursty, unpredictable load. As a software engineer on this team, you'll design and build systems that start and manage live streams for millions of viewers worldwide — working on systems that sit behind the customer-facing APIs and make every live stream possible.

- Own the technical direction of one or more services in the Stream Management portfolio; write the design docs, socialize them across IVS and adjacent teams, and drive them to implementation.
- Work closely with engineers, product managers, and applied scientists to deliver seamless customer experiences.
- Ensure backend systems are highly available, scalable, and secure at AWS scale.
- Apply backend best practices including testing, performance optimization, observability, and maintainable code.
- Collaborate with other AWS service teams to integrate shared services and deliver consistent AWS service experiences.
- Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, design reviews, and on-call rotations.
- Drive operational excellence through automation, metrics, alarms, and runbooks.
- Lead post-incident investigations for high-severity events in our services; drive the resulting action items to completion.

A day in the life

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS OpenSearch Service
jobs.description:
Imagine running search and analytics at any scale without thinking about clusters, capacity, or version upgrades. Where your queries return in milliseconds whether you're indexing a thousand documents or a hundred billion. Where the platform scales, heals, and secures itself so your team can focus on the questions, not the infrastructure.

That's what we build.

Amazon OpenSearch Service is the fully managed and Serverless AWS service that lets customers deploy, operate, and scale OpenSearch for log analytics, full-text search, application monitoring, observability, and AI-powered retrieval. We serve hundreds of thousands of customers running mission-critical workloads across every AWS region, and we are part of the AWS Database and Analytics organization.

Come join the OpenSearch Control Plane team. We are responsible for a service that:

- Reliably manages a large fleet of cloud-native OpenSearch clusters and collections, freeing customers from sizing, scaling, and patching decisions
- Guarantees high availability and durability for mission-critical search and observability workloads at the scale of the most demanding internet businesses
- Orchestrates and automates the complete lifecycle of an OpenSearch cluster or collection — from creation through scale-up, scale-out, upgrade, replication, and fail-over

The OpenSearch control plane is not just any distributed system. It orchestrates a fleet of clusters across every AWS region, detects and recovers from node failures in seconds, and serves workloads that span petabytes of customer data. Most recently, we launched **OpenSearch Serverless NextGen** — delivering ultra-fast collection provisioning and true scale-to-zero capacity, so customers pay only for what they use and get a working environment in seconds rather than minutes. We are not done; this is one of many investments raising the bar for what customers can expect from a managed search service.

OpenSearch itself is a community-driven, Apache 2.0–licensed open-source search and analytics suite built on Apache Lucene. Since launching in July 2021, the project has delivered multiple major and minor releases advancing core search, vector search, and analytics. Our next phase focuses on transforming OpenSearch into an intelligent retrieval engine — one that meets the evolving needs of customers running search, analytics, and AI-powered workloads across structured, unstructured, and multi-modal data.

We work in Java, Rust, Python, and Go. We contribute upstream to OpenSearch and Apache Lucene. We are customer-obsessed, operate with the entrepreneurial pace of a startup inside one of the world's largest cloud providers, and value strong intuition backed by metrics.

**Operations is core engineering on this team, not overhead.** Engineers operate what they build, and we treat customer-impacting incidents with the same engineering rigor we apply to feature work. Reliability and Static Stability is a forcing function for design, not a phase after launch.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and operate components of a large-scale distributed control plane — reason about failure modes, multi-tenant isolation, and blast-radius before writing code
- Look for opportunities to simplify — consolidate duplicate abstractions, remove dead code, reduce configuration sprawl, and challenge complexity that doesn't earn its keep
- Treat operations as core engineering — own the systems you build end-to-end, participate fully in incident response and RCAs, and drive operational improvements that reduce cost and maintenance burden
- Solve real problems in cluster orchestration, capacity provisioning, lifecycle workflows, multi-tenant infrastructure, query routing, and operational tooling
- Use AI coding assistants and GenAI tools effectively across the software development lifecycle — from design and prototyping through coding, testing, code review, debugging, and operations — applying engineering judgment to validate AI-generated output against Amazon's correctness, security, and operational bar
- Write robust, efficient, and maintainable code in Java, Rust, Python, or Go
- Partner with senior engineers to translate ambiguous requirements into concrete deliverables; prototype, test, and validate
- Continually challenge what exists and explore what should change to better serve customers

jobs.title: Software Engineer II - AI/ML, AWS Neuron
jobs.description:
The Annapurna Labs team at Amazon builds AWS Neuron, the software development kit used to accelerate deep learning and GenAI workloads on Amazon’s custom machine learning accelerators, Inferentia and Trainium.

The AWS Neuron SDK, developed by the Annapurna Labs team at AWS, is the backbone for accelerating deep learning and GenAI workloads on Amazon's Inferentia and Trainium ML accelerators. This comprehensive toolkit includes an ML compiler, runtime, and application framework that seamlessly integrates with popular ML frameworks like PyTorch and JAX enabling unparalleled ML inference and training performance.

The Inference Enablement and Acceleration team is at the forefront of running a wide range of models and supporting novel architecture alongside maximizing their performance for AWS's custom ML accelerators. Working across the stack from PyTorch till the hardware-software boundary, our engineers build systematic infrastructure, innovate new methods and create high-performance kernels for ML functions, ensuring every compute unit is fine tuned for optimal performance for our customers' demanding workloads. We combine deep hardware knowledge with ML expertise to push the boundaries of what's possible in AI acceleration.

As part of the broader Neuron organization, our team works across multiple technology layers - from frameworks and kernels and collaborate with compiler to runtime and collectives. We not only optimize current performance but also contribute to future architecture designs, working closely with customers to enable their models and ensure optimal performance. This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of machine learning, high-performance computing, and distributed architectures, where you'll help shape the future of AI acceleration technology

You will architect and implement business critical features, and mentor a brilliant team of experienced engineers. We operate in spaces that are very large, yet our teams remain small and agile. There is no blueprint. We're inventing. We're experimenting. It is a very unique learning culture. The team works closely with customers on their model enablement, providing direct support and optimization expertise to ensure their machine learning workloads achieve optimal performance on AWS ML accelerators. The team collaborates with open source ecosystems to provide seamless integration and bring peak performance at scale for customers and developers.

This role is responsible for development, enablement and performance tuning of a wide variety of LLM model families, including massive scale large language models like the Llama family, DeepSeek and beyond. The Inference Enablement and Acceleration team works side by side with compiler engineers and runtime engineers to create, build and tune distributed inference solutions with Trainium and Inferentia. Experience optimizing inference performance for both latency and throughput on such large models across the stack from system level optimizations through to Pytorch or JAX is a must have.

You can learn more about Neuron
https://awsdocs-neuron.readthedocs-hosted.com/en/latest/neuron-guide/neuron-cc/index.html
https://aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/neuron/
https://github.com/aws/aws-neuron-sdk
https://www.amazon.science/how-silicon-innovation-became-the-secret-sauce-behind-awss-success

Key job responsibilities
This role will help lead the efforts in building distributed inference support for Pytorch in the Neuron SDK. This role will tune these models to ensure highest performance and maximize the efficiency of them running on the customer AWS Trainium and Inferentia silicon and servers. Strong software development using Python, System level programming and ML knowledge are both critical to this role. Our engineers collaborate across compiler, runtime, framework, and hardware teams to optimize machine learning workloads for our global customer base. Working at the intersection of software, hardware, and machine learning systems, you'll bring expertise in low-level optimization, system architecture, and ML model acceleration. In this role, you will:

* Design, develop, and optimize machine learning models and frameworks for deployment on custom ML hardware accelerators.
* Participate in all stages of the ML system development lifecycle including distributed computing based architecture design, implementation, performance profiling, hardware-specific optimizations, testing and production deployment.
* Build infrastructure to systematically analyze and onboard multiple models with diverse architecture.
* Design and implement high-performance kernels and features for ML operations, leveraging the Neuron architecture and programming models
* Analyze and optimize system-level performance across multiple generations of Neuron hardware
* Conduct detailed performance analysis using profiling tools to identify and resolve bottlenecks
* Implement optimizations such as fusion, sharding, tiling, and scheduling
* Conduct comprehensive testing, including unit and end-to-end model testing with continuous deployment and releases through pipelines.
* Work directly with customers to enable and optimize their ML models on AWS accelerators
* Collaborate across teams to develop innovative optimization techniques

A day in the life
You will collaborate with a cross-functional team of applied scientists, system engineers, and product managers to deliver state-of-the-art inference capabilities for Generative AI applications. Your work will involve debugging performance issues, optimizing memory usage, and shaping the future of Neuron's inference stack across Amazon and the Open Source Community. As you design and code solutions to help our team drive efficiencies in software architecture, you’ll create metrics, implement automation and other improvements, and resolve the root cause of software defects.

You will also build high-impact solutions to deliver to our large customer base and participate in design discussions, code review, and communicate with internal and external stakeholders. You will work cross-functionally to help drive business decisions with your technical input. You will work in a startup-like development environment, where you’re always working on the most important initiative.

About the team
The Inference Enablement and Acceleration team fosters a builder’s culture where experimentation is encouraged, and impact is measurable. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Our senior members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future. jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer, Benefits Experience and Technology (BXT)
jobs.description:
Using your benefits today means portals, phone calls, hold music, and fine print. We are changing that by bringing AI in as a strategic partner: software that understands what a person needs and helps them find the answer at the moment of need. This posting is for the tech lead on one of our two biggest product bets, driving large, ambiguous problems that span multiple organizations. This is a generative-AI and agentic-engineering role first, at very large scale.

You will join Benefits Engagement Technology and Services (BETS), the Amazon organization reinventing how more than a million employees and their families engage with their benefits. Our vision is benefits that are AI-powered, personalized, and proactive, where timely guidance reaches people when they need it rather than making them hunt for it. BETS builds and operates the platform that delivers benefits experiences across mobile, web, and an AI assistant, from self-service content creation to multi-channel campaigns to analytics, and we are now building a family of AI-native products on top of it.
Two of those products are our biggest bets, and we are building each as a focused product team inside BETS:
- A reimagined health plan where AI is a strategic partner for members instead of a portal to navigate. Rather than directories, phone trees, and hold music, it understands what someone needs and brings the right answer to them at the moment of need: the in-network doctor, the real out-of-pocket cost before they book, the claim explained in plain language, and the next step taken on their behalf. It is built on secure, HIPAA-compliant foundations to serve very large member populations, with a path to serve other organizations over time.
- An agentic workforce for benefits operations that makes running benefits for a workforce of millions dramatically easier. Managing dozens of programs, vendors, and budgets is enormous operational work; AI agents take on that heavy lifting, surfacing what needs attention, preparing the analysis and the recommended action, and handling the routine, so the people who manage benefits spend their time on decisions and strategy instead of manual operations. The system learns from every decision and keeps that knowledge with the team.

You will be the tech lead on one of these two products.

Here is what sets this organization apart: we do not just build AI products, we build them the AI Native way, and we have already proven it. A small pod rebuilt a major benefits platform and shipped it to production in 3 months, work originally scoped at 12, by restructuring how we engineer around agents. In our model, humans own judgment and agents own the mechanical middle. Engineers write the specification and set the acceptance criteria; agents (Claude Code, Kiro) write a growing share of the implementation, author tests, and resolve code-review comments; engineers direct, validate, and own what ships, and still hand-write the novel, ambiguous, and infrastructure-heavy work where models fall short. Recursive self-improvement, where the system proposes its own next version and a human approves, is the north star we are deliberately climbing toward, one validated step at a time, with humans at the judgment gates.

As a Senior Software Development Engineer in BETS, you are the tech lead for your team’s product. You lead the software development of a system of many features across its full lifecycle, working shoulder to shoulder with peers on related teams, on problems where the customer direction is clear but the technology strategy is not and the constraints conflict and span multiple organizations. You own the team-level architecture and provide the system-wide view and design guidance, making the high-stakes, hard-to-reverse decisions and reviewing others’ work, human-authored and agent-authored alike, so it fits the bigger picture and is extensible, performant, and secure. You stay hands-on in the code and code reviews that matter most.

You lead the team’s adoption and evolution of the AI Native build loops (the specs, acceptance criteria, and simulation coverage that let agents safely take on more of the work, plus the scoped authorization and guardrails that travel with that autonomy) and shape the agentic foundations the team builds on, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and MCP. You drive operational excellence for a regulated, large-scale service, resolve root causes even when the fix crosses team boundaries, and are sought out by partner teams (identity, privacy, security, legal, and vendors) for your expertise. Above all, you grow the engineers around you: you lead through influence and constructive debate, coach and mentor multiple engineers, and set a quality bar the team emulates. The strongest technical leaders here work backwards from the customer and bring a strong product design sense, not just technical elegance, to every decision.

How we work, honestly: teams here are small, which means high ownership density and architectural decisions you will actually own rather than inherit fully formed. Some of our work carries hard, externally committed launch dates, so this role carries real deadline pressure. Because we handle sensitive personal data, privacy and security are designed in from the start and are everyone’s responsibility, not an afterthought. You own what you build, including its operations and on-call. In return you build rare, portable depth: regulated, large-scale platforms, production agentic systems, and the judgment to direct them.

This role is for tech leads who think like owners. If you want to prove that a small, senior team can enter a hard domain and win, if you want to design the systems that build systems, and if you are drawn to decisions that will still matter across the next several product generations, this is a rare seat.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead your team’s software development end to end: own the team-level architecture, provide the system-wide view and design guidance, make the high-stakes one-way-door decisions, and deliver a system of many features across its full lifecycle.
- Be the tech lead on large, ambiguous problems that span multiple organizations, where the customer direction is clear but the technology strategy is not; drive clarity and align partner teams (identity, privacy, security, legal, and vendors) on the path forward.
- Lead and mentor engineers: coach multiple engineers on and off your team, help grow the team through recruiting and career guidance, and drive adoption of engineering best practices that others emulate.
- Work backwards from the customer, bringing product design judgment to technical decisions, not just technical elegance.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Leo Autopilot
jobs.description:
Are you ready to write code that operates real spacecraft in orbit? We're building the autonomous system that decides what every satellite in our constellation does, when it does it, and how it recovers when something goes wrong — all without a human in the loop for routine operations. This isn't about building another web service; it's about creating software that continuously manages an entire fleet of satellites at scale, making critical decisions under real physical constraints.

This role offers a rare combination: the depth of hard systems problems — planning and scheduling under physical constraints, coordinating across a large fleet, designing safeguards you have to trust with spacecraft — alongside the ownership that comes with a small team and an expanding charter. Because the constellation and its software are both still growing, the architecture decisions you make now will run for the life of the fleet, and your work connects directly to delivering reliable broadband to people who don't have it today.

Export Control:

- Work with our peer teams and customers to design suitable software systems to fulfill the mission needs.
- Develop cloud native software systems in Java and Python.
- Utilize AWS and other Amazon technologies to build highly-available software services.
- Design and develop performant software systems that meet the mission criteria and requirements.
- Help on-board and mentor new team members.
- Lead technical roadmap definition efforts and decide which features and performance improvements to build.

A day in the life
You start the day with your team, aligning on what's shipping and where you can unblock each other. Most of your time goes to building: designing services, writing and reviewing code, and hardening systems that operate real spacecraft. You work closely with operators and mission teams, watching how they handle tricky situations, spotting patterns, and turning them into automation. Some weeks you go deep on a single system; others you're connecting several so they work as one. You'll also take turns supporting the systems you build, which keeps you close to how they behave in the real world.

About the team
Our mission is to operate a satellite constellation autonomously. We're building software that changes how satellites are managed: the ground sets the intent and guardrails, and the system schedules work, coordinates across the fleet, and recovers from faults on its own — with people supervising outcomes instead of issuing commands one at a time.

We're a small team with a large and expanding charter, which means engineers here have real influence over architecture and direction. We care about operational excellence, clear thinking, and building systems we can trust with spacecraft. You'll collaborate closely with operations, mission planning, and hardware teams, and you'll see your work make a direct difference for customers who don't have reliable broadband today.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Amazon Route 53, Route 53 DNS Firewall & Profiles
jobs.description:
Amazon Route 53 has an open position for a Software Development Engineer in Arlington, VA to join the team that designs, builds and operates Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and Route 53 Profiles.

We're looking for a mid-level Software Development Engineer to join our team. The team manages cloud-native DNS security and DNS resource management services that protect millions of VPCs from malicious domain activity and enable customers to centrally manage DNS configurations across their multi-account environments. You will be part of the team that ensures that DNS traffic is inspected, filtered, and governed securely, reliably, and at scale for enterprise customers running workloads across VPCs, hybrid networks, and multi-account organizations. Along with the team you will design and build new solutions for the services, models for detecting new threats and attacks by working with stakeholders across the company and with our external partners.

Key job responsibilities
As an SDE, you will work across the entire stack—control plane, data plane, API surfaces, and deep integrations with Route 53 Resolver, VPC networking, Private Link, AWS RAM, AWS Firewall Manager, and AWS Organizations. You will design and build advanced detection features, enhance configurability for customers, and help architect next-generation protections including agentic attack prevention capabilities. You will also help drive system architecture, spearhead best practices that enable a quality product, and help coach and develop junior engineers. A successful candidate will have an established background in engineering large-scale distributed systems or networking software, great communication skills, and a motivation to achieve results in a fast-paced environment.

A day in the life
At Amazon Web Services, we like to "work backwards": we start by understanding what customers need and use that to guide our software engineering. We're looking for a software engineer who is experienced in listening to customers, synthesizing their needs, and rapidly iterating our services to quickly put features into customers' hands. Our best ideas become even better when we get feedback from real customer use. The sooner we can get that feedback, the more quickly we can grow.

On a typical day, you might investigate a DNS threat pattern to improve detection accuracy, prototype a new filtering capability, instrument code to report security metrics, collaborate with partner teams on integration designs, code up a feature for centralized profile management, or draft a proposal for a new agentic protection capability.

About the team
This team designs, builds and operates the high availability enterprise scale DNS Firewall service along with Route 53 Profiles. DNS Firewall provides DNS-layer protection natively using models designed and built by the team and through partnerships with major DNS security providers. Route 53 Profiles enables customers to apply DNS-related configurations—including Resolver rules, DNS Firewall rule groups, and private hosted zone associations—across multiple VPCs with a single, shareable configuration. Together, these services form a critical part of AWS's network security and governance story, serving customers ranging from startups to the largest enterprises.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Marketing Measurement and Performance Science
jobs.description:
Marketing Measurement and Performance Science (MAPS) measures the incremental impact of Amazon's marketing investments on customer perception, action, and purchases — covering billions in annual fixed marketing (FM) spend across the full funnel. Our outputs provide spend insights and recommendations that power total investment decisions at the S-team level for OP planning, BU-level budget allocation, and in-year spend guidance.

As an SDE II, you'll design and build the systems that transform and harmonize data from 20+ external partners — each with their own schemas, grains, cadences, and nuances — into the measurement-grade inputs that power COSMOS, Amazon's FM causal measurement framework. The problems you will coverage go beyond standard ETL responsibilities — you'll build AI-native systems that reconcile providers with incompatible definitions, handle split metric ownership, manage retroactive revisions, and maintain the immutable snapshots and deterministic joins that causal inference demands.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and maintain measurement-grade data systems at scale — ingesting, standardizing, and vending marketing data from 20+ external and internal sources that feed causal modeling and MLOps systems.
- Own full lifecycle delivery of production software on complex, ambiguous problems — from design through launch and ongoing operations — with independence and minimal guidance.
- Build automated validation pipelines and data quality frameworks that enforce contracts, detect anomalies across providers, and ensure measurement-grade integrity at every stage.
- Define statistical methods for outlier detection, diagnose root causes systematically, and determine corrective actions to maintain data trust.
- Partner across science, product, and engineering teams to scope solutions, navigate constraints, and ship the most efficient path from prototype to production.
- Write clean, well-tested code (Python, Scala, or Java) and mentor junior engineers on system design, code quality, and operational best practices.

A day in the life
Day to day, you'll build and scale multi-layer automated validation pipelines, with clear data lineage so every model run is fully reproducible. Our vision is to scale our infrastructure across new business units and geographies reaching 90%+ coverage of Amazon's FM spend, and develop self-service catalog and observability tooling that lets scientists and partner teams explore our data without filing tickets. You'll also have a direct influence on schema governance — designing systems that enforce data standards at the point of contract, detect drift from providers, and keep our specifications current as partnerships expand.

You'll collaborate closely with causal scientists, economists, product managers, and agency data ops teams — translating measurement requirements into scalable technical solutions. This is a high-ownership role where your work directly determines whether Amazon's leadership can trust the numbers behind billion-dollar marketing investment decisions.


About the team
Within MAPS, the Marketing Inputs & Data Automation (MIDA) team owns the measurement-grade data layer that sets the ceiling on what our causal models can measure, where they can operate, and how confident leadership should be in the outputs. We build and operate large-scale data infrastructure and data assets — ingesting, validating, harmonizing, and vending data from 20+ third-party providers (agencies, aggregators, publishers) across multiple Amazon business units and marketing channels, with global coverage. Our pipeline is purpose-built for the high bar of causal inference — not dashboards or reporting — requiring strict temporal integrity, historical stability, multi-layer validation, full lineage, and reproducibility at every stage.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer II, SCOT-Fulfillment Optimization (FO): Outbound Optimization
jobs.description:
Have you ever ordered a product on Amazon and wondered how it got to you so fast? Did you ever think about how Amazon decides which warehouse to ship from, or whether your items should come in one box or two?

Join us in building the real-time optimization systems that make these decisions — rebalancing millions of shipment assignments every hour across Amazon's US fulfillment network to deliver packages faster,
cheaper, and more efficiently.

The Outbound Optimization (O2) team, within Fulfillment Optimization (FO), is responsible for developing and operating the systems that improve upon initial fulfillment assignments at a network level. Our flagship system processes all candidate shipments in the country's network hourly, optimizing for plan adherence, delivery speed, capacity utilization, and cost — directly impacting billions of dollars in annual fulfillment spend. We
are seeking a talented, driven Software Development Engineer.

As an SDE II for O2:
- You will design and build distributed optimization pipelines, partner with applied scientists to translate mathematical models into production systems, and own end-to-end delivery of features that have immediate, measurable business impact.
- You will work with research scientists, engineers, and peers to design, develop, test and deploy technology that supports our quickly evolving and growing operations.

This role is a highly visible and critical position within Amazon with significant customer impact. A successful candidate will have an established background in building distributed systems, strong technical ability, and a motivation to achieve results in a fast-paced environment.

Key job responsibilities
In this role, you will:
- Design and build distributed compute pipelines that process hundreds of millions of shipments per optimization run
- Partner with applied scientists to productionize optimization models (Lagrangian decomposition, constraint programming)
- Own and operate production services across AWS (Lambda, Fargate, ECS on EC2)
- Build new optimization levers — cost dimensions, constraints, and demand models in OPC
- Develop data pipelines and validation tooling to measure business impact of optimization decisions
- Exercise judgment in making technical tradeoffs between solution quality, latency, and system complexity

A day in the life
As an SDE II on O2, you might spend your morning whiteboarding with an applied scientist on how to model a new optimization objective, then spend the afternoon turning that math into Kotlin code that will
reassign millions of packages across the network. One week you're designing a new cost dimension that penalizes early shipments to unlock consolidation opportunities; the next you're building a combinatorial algorithm that generates fulfillment options faster than a commercial solver. You'll deploy your changes, watch them flow through simulations and see the business impact in dashboards within days.

You own problems end-to-end — from the math to the code to production. Your decisions directly move metrics on billions of dollars of shipment flow, and you'll feel that weight and reward daily. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment.

The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:
- Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
- Maternity and Parental Leave Options
- Paid Time Off (PTO)
- 401(k) Plan

If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you!

At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

jobs.description:

Watch this video to learn more about our organization, SCOT: http://bit.ly/amazon-scot

Amazon's Supply Chain Optimization Technologies (SCOT) organization is responsible for the end-to-end systems that plan, optimize, and execute the movement of billions of packages across the world's most complex logistics network. We build real-time, intelligent, and fully automated systems that touch every aspect of the delivery experience from the moment a customer clicks "Buy" to the package arriving at their door.

What you'll work on:
- You'll join a team within SCOT that's pushing the boundaries of what's possible with AI and algorithms in transportation:
- AI-Powered Network Automation – Build agentic AI systems that continuously monitor, optimize, and autonomously evolve one of the world's largest transportation networks. You'll work on systems that generate, validate, and deploy network configurations using large language models and advanced automation moving toward a future where the network intelligently adapts itself.
- Route Optimization at Scale – Design and implement graph algorithms that find optimal routes across a massive, multi-modal transportation network optimizing simultaneously for speed, cost, and environmental sustainability. You'll solve multi-variable optimization problems at a scale few companies in the world operate at.
- Scalable Distributed Systems – Build highly available, low-latency services that process millions of decisions in real-time, powering the backbone of Amazon's transportation planning and execution

What we're looking for:

- Strong foundations in data structures, algorithms, and system design
- Experience with or passion for: graph algorithms, optimization, AI/ML systems, or generative AI
- Ability to break down ambiguous, complex problems into elegant, shippable solutions
- Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where you own your systems end-to-end
- Excellent communication skills and a track record of raising the engineering bar on your team

Key job responsibilities
You will be working on a high throughput system that deals with complex challenges in the field of distributed systems and math optimization. You will be responsible for:
1. Leading end to end design of core infrastructural improvements
2. Leading discussions with business teams, supply chain managers and other experts in the field of supply chain and logistics to model ground realities into software
3. Building scalable mechanisms to deal with operational load, continous improvement systems to monitor and reduce defects, and mechanisms to manage complex operations while running lean systems

About the team
Within Amazon's Supply Chain Optimization Technologies, the F2P (Fulfill to Promise) team makes assignment decisions for every customer order fulfilled by the Amazon fulfillment network.

These decisions are customer-obsessed: they prioritize customer needs and satisfaction, then minimize fulfillment cost. Because the KPIs tracking fulfillment cost naturally trade off against one another, and because Amazon's speed and selection offerings constantly evolve, the team builds scalable mechanisms that model these offerings and balance their trade-offs when making assignment decisions.

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer II, UTR Tech
jobs.description:
Amazon’s global fulfilment network enables any merchant in any of the geography ship items that you order on Amazon, to any place on earth. Amazon Logistics’ (AMZL) delivery stations (DS) receive packages from Fulfilment Centers (FCs) and Sort Centers (SCs) and sort them to route level. Drivers come into the DS and pick up the packages for their route and deliver them to Amazon’s customers. This operation is also called the “Last Mile”. An integral component in the Last Mile ecosystem are Amazon's WW delivery hubs where packages are received, sorted and prepared for on-road delivery. Station Tech team, in Last Mile, is responsible for building scalable tools and technology for delivery hubs that scale across multiple programs and businesses including Amazon Logistics (AMZL), Global Specialty Fulfilment (GSF), to increase associate productivity, site throughput, and operational quality and scalability of our delivery network. Our primary customers are delivery station associates (our actual on-ground rockstars who sort millions of packages a day), station managers (who manage Amazon hubs WW to ensure customer promises are met), COs (central operations team who supervise stations across regions) and on-road delivery agents (drivers who sail through all obstacles to get your packages at your doorstep). The team build tools and process which guide our customers to reduce their cognitive load, eliminate decision points to drive standardisation, prioritise work to focus on the highest impact tasks, and take steps for correcting operational defects to reduce the impact of human error and meet our customer SLAs.

UTR Tech is an organisation within Last Mile supporting all the delivery stations in the delivery network. A delivery station receives an input set of packages from upstream and performs the required set of operations and processes on the packages to ultimately get them out of the delivery stations for on-road delivery. The associates within the delivery stations use a mobile based application called Dolphin for running the execution operations. As an SDE II on the UTR Tech team, you'll build and scale the systems powering Amazon's fastest delivery promises - Same-Day Delivery (SSD), Grocery, and Rush (1-hr/3-hr) programs across NA, EU, JP, and the Middle East. You'll own services spanning package injection, staging, sortation, and routing that keep millions of time-critical orders on-time, and directly move quality metrics like slot-level DEA and defect BPS. This role blends deep technical ownership with high operational impact: your code runs in a live, sub-hour delivery network where reliability and latency are non-negotiable. You'll partner with product, science, and operations to launch new speed programs and expand grocery (including perishable/chill-chain) into new regions. We're looking for an engineer who thrives on distributed-systems challenges at scale and wants their work to be visible to customers the same day.

Key job responsibilities
As an Engineer in the team, you will take part in in the architecture, design, implementation and deployment of large-scale and complex software systems. You will get to leverage your experience and expertise to deliver innovative solutions to challenging problems. You will communicate your ideas effectively to achieve the right outcome for your team and customer. You enjoy collaborating with others to increase the effectiveness of the overall team. Your code, design, and implementation decisions should set a great example to other engineers. You will also have the opportunity to impact the technical decisions in the broader organization as well as mentor other engineers in the team.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Creative Asset Library, CreativeX
jobs.description:
We own both sides of the ad creative experience for Amazon DSP, the advertiser experience (AX) where advertisers build and manage creatives across display, video, and streaming TV, and the customer experience (CX) where those creatives render and deliver personalized content to hundreds of millions of shoppers at impression time. - Design and implement software solutions that enable new features and improve existing systems, applying sound judgment when making tradeoffs between scalability, maintainability, performance, and security.
- Own the full development lifecycle for major portions of your team's software, including scoping, coding, testing, deployment, and operational support, ensuring root causes of issues are identified and permanently resolved.

- Collaborate with customers, stakeholders, and peers to understand business and customer value, ensuring solutions address real needs while evaluating opportunities to leverage generative artificial intelligence tools where appropriate.
- Participate actively in code reviews, providing meaningful feedback to engineers across experience levels, and mentor teammates on producing high-quality, maintainable code.

About the team
The team owns the central creative asset platform for Amazon Ads - the universal repository where advertisers upload once and activate everywhere across display, video, OLV, streaming TV, and audio. We operate services that power the advertiser-facing UIs, media processing pipelines, and 3P ingestion services that scale worldwide. We're replacing today's fragmented per-format silos with standardized primitives that work across all Amazon Ads surfaces, building end-to-end asset management for every ad creative format. You'll also work upstream, expressing requirements and constraints that the core R&D team needs to be aware of so their work can ultimately be certified.

If you want to own the software that stands between robots and the people around them and take it all the way from research prototype to certified product, then this role is for you.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the library of safety-critical embedded software modules, taking full responsibility for their quality, maintainability, and certification readiness
• Translate R&D algorithm code from the core development team into production-grade, certifiable embedded software that meets functional safety standards
• Define and communicate software requirements and constraints upstream to the core R&D team, ensuring their algorithm development is compatible with certification objectives
• Drive the software through the full safety certification lifecycle, producing the code, documentation, and evidence required for formal certification

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, AWS Applied AI Solutions
jobs.description:
As part of the AWS Applied AI Solutions organization, we have a vision to provide business applications, leveraging Amazon’s unique experience and expertise, that are used by millions of companies worldwide to manage day-to-day operations. We will accomplish this by accelerating our customers’ businesses through delivery of intuitive and differentiated technology solutions that solve enduring business challenges. We blend vision with curiosity and Amazon’s real-world experience to build opinionated, turnkey solutions. Where customers prefer to buy over build, we become their trusted partner with solutions that are no-brainers to buy and easy to use.

On Agentic WorkSpaces, our vision is to enable AI agents to work the way humans do: with access to real applications, real interfaces, and real computing environments. For enterprises to trust autonomous agents with their essential business applications, they need to see what agents did, control what agents can do, and prove both to auditors. Our team builds the systems that make this possible. We record every agent desktop action as a reviewable visual audit trail, enforce policy on every tool call before it executes, pause agents for human approval on sensitive actions, and package the evidence for compliance frameworks.

We are seeking an exceptional Senior SDE to own the identity architecture at the foundation of this system. When an agent acts inside a user's desktop session, it inherits that user's identity. Every downstream system then attributes the agent's actions to the human. Solving this means deciding how agent identity is established, propagated across protocol and service boundaries, and preserved through to policy enforcement and audit. These decisions determine whether the rest of the governance stack — attribution, enforcement, approval, evidence — can be trusted at all. You will make foundational architectural calls, write code, mentor the engineers around you, and drive consensus with partner teams whose identity models were built for humans. This is a high-visibility, high-ownership role on a small team solving problems with no established playbook. If you do your best work in ambiguity and want your technical decisions to set the direction for how enterprises govern AI agents, this team is for you.

Key job responsibilities
* Own the end-to-end identity architecture for agent governance: how agent identity is established, propagated, and preserved across desktop sessions, protocol boundaries, and downstream services

* Design attribution and audit systems that distinguish agent actions from human actions within the same session, at the infrastructure level where agents cannot tamper with the record

* Own policy enforcement architecture, including authorization models that evaluate agent actions before they execute

* Evaluate build-vs-leverage decisions across identity and authorization primitives, including assessments of existing internal and external components for reuse

* Drive technical consensus with partner teams whose identity and permission models predate autonomous agents

* Mentor and develop junior and mid-level engineers through code reviews and design reviews

* Communicate architectural decisions and tradeoffs to senior leadership and non-technical stakeholders

A day in the life
Your mornings are usually free for focus work — architecture, deep dives, and hard problems. Around 11 you'll have standup, then grab lunch with the team (if you like) before the afternoon opens up for design reviews, CR feedback, or unblocking an engineer. Some days you're deep in code; others you're presenting to leadership. You're the person who knows the system most deeply — and you work to ensure you're never the bottleneck. The problems are hard and the stakes are high — but we believe we can move fast, do exceptional work, and have a full life outside of it.

We're a small team building two greenfield projects within Agentic WorkSpaces. We're moving fast enough that our team name is still taking shape — but our engineering culture is well established. Here's what you can expect from AWS:

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, GNC Software, Amazon Leo
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Amazon Leo is an ambitious project that depends on entirely new satellite designs along with all of the ground capabilities needed to operate a large constellation and provide high performance service to end users. Because the constellation will have several thousand satellites serving millions of customers, systems are being designed to be highly autonomous, self-adaptable to the environment, and capable of recovery in the event of problems. The great majority of new equipment and software is being developed and built in-house by our engineering and manufacturing teams.

Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) designs the constellation for good coverage and space safety, and develops the systems that control and maneuver each satellite as they ascend from injection to operational orbits, merge into the constellation flow and station keep relative to neighbors. Every spacecraft is ready and able to maneuver at any time to avoid other satellites or space debris if a close pass threatens.

The navigation system provides precise positioning in real-time and supports forecasting future orbital state, taking into account planned maneuvers and other effects. Guidance, Navigation, and Control also provides cueing to direct the communications systems on the satellite that require accurate pointing in order to achieve high performance.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
As a Guidance, Navigation, and Control software engineer, you will develop real-time, embedded software that flies the satellite; ground-based applications that predict orbital state, monitor for potential collisions, and optimize maneuvers; high fidelity modeling and simulation software; and all sorts of infrastructure needed to develop and operate the system. Because GNC is the heart of the satellite flight system, you will frequently be pulled in to help with a broad spectrum of problems standing in the way of satellite integration and test, manufacturing, and even flight operations.

A day in the life
This is an opportunity to play a significant role in the design of an entirely new satellite system with challenging performance requirements. The large, integrated constellation brings opportunities for advanced capabilities that need investigation and development. Scale also puts emphasis on engineering excellence so our tools and methods, from conceptualization through manufacturing and all phases of test, will be state of the art as will the satellite and supporting infrastructure on the ground. You will split time working well defined SW projects needed by the program on a schedule, prototyping design concepts that may or may not make it to production, participating in component and satellite level testing, and helping with flight operations.

About the team
Our team has experience with various satellite systems and many other flight vehicles. We have bench strength in our mission, the core Guidance, Navigation, and Control disciplines, and software development for flight and other systems. We design, prototype, test, iterate and learn together. Because GNC is central to safe flight, we tend to drive Concepts of Operation and many system level analyses. You will find that Amazon Leo's mission is compelling, so our program is staffed with some of the top engineers in the industry. Our daily collaboration with other teams on the program brings constant opportunity for discovery, learning, and growth.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Agentic Workspaces - Watchtower
jobs.description:
As part of the AWS Applied AI Solutions organization, we have a vision to provide business applications, leveraging Amazon’s unique experience and expertise, that are used by millions of companies worldwide to manage day-to-day operations. We will accomplish this by accelerating our customers’ businesses through delivery of intuitive and differentiated technology solutions that solve enduring business challenges. We blend vision with curiosity and Amazon’s real-world experience to build opinionated, turnkey solutions. Where customers prefer to buy over build, we become their trusted partner with solutions that are no-brainers to buy and easy to use.

Amazon WorkSpaces has protected and empowered enterprise work for over a decade, and we are now reimagining what a workspace is. We are building Agentic WorkSpaces: a platform where the workspace itself is an active partner in how you work, not just infrastructure that delivers applications. Today more than a million users rely on WorkSpaces daily; tomorrow those workSpaces will host AI agents alongside humans, agents that code, troubleshoot, analyze, and act on behalf of their users, governed by the same identity and security policies as the people they serve. We compete with Microsoft, Citrix, and Omnissa, and we intend to leapfrog them by building the workspace that was designed for the agentic era, not retrofitted for it.

Agentic WorkSpaces' Watchtower team is the layer that makes this possible from the inside of every WorkSpace: telemetry, health, secure communications both inbound and outbound, Agentic AI platforms for qualification of Operating System, Instance and Applications. Our mission is to provide robust monitoring, automation, and operational capabilities that ensure the reliability and performance of WorkSpaces Instances.
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to design, build, and operate the services, secure, and maintain WorkSpaces for humans and, increasingly, for the AI agents that work beside them, across every supported OS and identity provider. You will own end-to-end delivery of features and systems within Watchtower - from design through deployment and operations - holding a high bar for availability, latency, and security.

You are customer-obsessed, technically deep, and energized by solving hard problems. You think big about what the workspace of the future looks like - a unified agent shipping to two platforms from one codebase, an identity model that treats humans and agents as first-class citizens, and autonomous troubleshooting that resolves issues before users notice - and then you build the systems to get there. You thrive in ambiguity, make sound trade-off decisions with incomplete information, and hold yourself accountable for results that matter. You want to solve challenging problems in operating systems, identity, AI, and desktop platform engineering at a scale that impacts more than a million users daily.

Key job responsibilities
In our team, you will indulge your love of diving deep into complex technical problems, driving incremental system optimizations and raising the bar for operational excellence and development practices. We will look to you to help enhance the skills and expertise of those around you.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
